title: Lurbinectedin Injection
overview: Lurbinectedin injection is used to treat small cell lung cancer (SCLC) that has spread to other parts of the body and did not improve during or after treatment with platinum chemotherapy. Lurbinectedin injection is in a class of medications called alkylating agents. It works by slowing or stopping the growth of cancer cells in your body.

sections.Before receiving lurbinectedin injection: tell your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to lurbinectedin, any other medications, or any of the ingredients in lurbinectedin injection. Ask your pharmacist for a list of the ingredients.tell your doctor and pharmacist what other prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, or nutritional supplements you are taking or plan to take. Your doctor may need to change the doses of your medications or monitor you carefully for side effects.The following nonprescription or herbal products may interact with lurbinectedin: St. John's wort. Be sure to let your doctor and pharmacist know that you are taking this medication before you start receiving lurbinectedin injection. Do not start this medication while receiving lurbinectedin injection without discussing with your healthcare provider.tell your doctor if you have or have ever had liver or kidney disease.tell your doctor if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or if you plan to father a child. You or your partner should not become pregnant while you are receiving lurbinectedin injection. Your doctor may perform a pregnancy test to be sure that you are not pregnant before you receive lurbinectedin injection. If you are female, you should use birth control during your treatment and for 6 months after your final dose. If you are male, you and your female partner should use birth control during your treatment and for 4 months after your final dose. If you or your partner become pregnant while receiving lurbinectedin injection, call your doctor. Lurbinectedin injection may harm the fetus.tell your doctor if you are breast-feeding. You should not breast-feed while you are receiving lurbinectedin injection and for at least 2 weeks after your final dose.
sections.Lurbinectedin may cause side effects. Te: fatiguenauseavomitingconstipationdiarrhealoss of appetitejoint or bone painheadachetingling, numbness, and pain in the hands and feet
sections.Some side effects can be serious. If you: chest painshortness of breathlight-colored bowel movements, yellowing of the skin or eyes, loss of appetite, dark yellow or brown urine, or pain in the upper right part of stomachunusual bleeding or bruisingfever, cough, chills, or other signs of infectiontiredness or pale skinsevere muscle pain or weaknessLurbinectedin may cause other side effects. Call your doctor if you have any unusual problems while receiving this medication.If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may send a report to the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online (https://www.fda.gov/Safety/MedWatch) or by phone (1-800-332-1088).
